  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: add a shasum fallback: gate_sup_token_fp="$(printf '%s|%s' "${GH_TOKEN:-}" "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" | (sha256sum || shasum -a 256) 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-64)". Estimated lines changed: 2.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:header comment block at lines 80-93
  PROBLEM: (Hardening suggestion, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1) The header comment documents the new PR_CHECKS_GATE_SUPERSEDED log line but not the two new shell-global cache variables PR_CHECKS_GATE_SUP_SELF_LOGIN_CACHE and PR_CHECKS_GATE_SUP_SELF_LOGIN_CACHE_KEY.
  WHY: A future caller who reads only the header cannot tell that these variables exist or that they persist across calls in the same shell. Suggested minimal fix: add a short header block covering four points. The first variable holds the cached login. The second holds the sha256 fingerprint of GH_TOKEN|GITHUB_TOKEN that keys it. Both are written only on a successful, regex-matching GET user read, and a failed or invalid read is never cached. Both persist across _pr_checks_completed calls in the same shell. Estimated lines changed: 6-8.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:gate_sup_token_fp computation around line 481
  PROBLEM: (Hardening suggestion, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1) The fingerprint uses only sha256sum, so on systems that ship only shasum -a 256 (stock macOS, some minimal containers) it comes back empty.
  WHY: With an empty key, `[ -n "${gate_sup_token_fp}" ]` is false at both the cache-check and cache-update sites. The cache then silently never engages and every poll repeats GET user, which is the rate-limit behaviour the previous autofix run was meant to remove. Suggested fix: if the result is empty, fall back to `shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-64` (or openssl dgst -sha256). Estimated lines changed: 2-3.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:line 481 (`gate_sup_token_fp="$(printf '%s|%s' "${GH_TOKEN:-}" "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" | sha256sum 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-64)"`)
  PROBLEM: (Hardening suggestion, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1) sha256sum is part of GNU coreutils. On systems that ship only `shasum -a 256` (e.g. local macOS runs of `review_rb_judge.sh` / `unblock_judge.sh`), the pipe fails, `2>/dev/null` hides the error, and the fingerprint stays empty.
  WHY: The cache then never engages and every merge-wait poll repeats the `GET user` read. Suggested minimal fix: if `gate_sup_token_fp` is empty after `sha256sum`, fall back to `shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-64`. Estimated lines changed: 2.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:header comment block, lines 83-90
  PROBLEM: (Hardening suggestion, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1) The two new globals `PR_CHECKS_GATE_SUP_SELF_LOGIN_CACHE` / `PR_CHECKS_GATE_SUP_SELF_LOGIN_CACHE_KEY` are documented only in an inline comment at line 474, not in the header block that documents the other `PR_CHECKS_*` variables (see lines 45-82).
  WHY: A future editor reading only the header would not know these variables exist or that they are written once per token. Suggested minimal fix: add a short header paragraph that names both variables. It should say the first holds the cached self login and the second holds the sha256 fingerprint of `GH_TOKEN|GITHUB_TOKEN` that keys it. It should also say both are written only after a successful, regex-valid `GET user` read, that a failed read is never cached, and that both persist across `_pr_checks_completed` calls in the same shell. Estimated lines changed: 5.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
